definition: difficult to understand; obscure
example: The professor's abstruse lecture left even the graduate students bewildered.

definition: sharp and biting in tone or manner
example: Her acerbic review spared neither the director nor the cast.

definition: cheerful readiness or eagerness
example: He accepted the challenge with alacrity.

definition: something or someone intensely disliked or loathed
example: Compromise was anathema to the senator.

definition: of doubtful authenticity, though widely circulated as true
example: The story of the founder's humble origins is probably apocryphal.

definition: formal approval or praise
example: The proposal won the committee's enthusiastic approbation.

definition: practicing severe self-discipline and avoiding indulgence
example: He led an ascetic life, eating little and owning less.

definition: to make an unpleasant feeling less intense; to soothe
example: Her calm tone did little to assuage his fears.

definition: stubbornly resistant to authority or control
example: The recalcitrant student refused every request to revise the essay.

definition: deliberately faithless; treacherous
example: The perfidious aide leaked the plan to the rival camp.

definition: excessively eager to please or obey
example: The obsequious assistant laughed at every one of his boss's jokes.

definition: harmful in a gradual or subtle way
example: The pernicious rumor slowly destroyed her reputation.

definition: having keen insight; mentally sharp
example: A perspicacious investor, she spotted the flaw in the pitch at once.

definition: lacking courage; timid
example: The pusillanimous mayor avoided every controversial vote.

definition: extremely idealistic and impractical
example: Their quixotic plan to end all traffic seemed doomed.

definition: little known or understood; abstruse
example: The scholar's recondite references baffled the general reader.

definition: having sound judgment and wisdom
example: A sagacious negotiator, she knew when to stay silent.

definition: optimistic, especially in a difficult situation
example: Despite the setbacks, he remained sanguine about the project.

definition: a person who flatters the powerful to gain advantage
example: The CEO surrounded himself with sycophants who never disagreed.

definition: habitually silent or reserved in speech
example: The taciturn farmer answered questions in single words.

definition: promoting a particular, often controversial, point of view
example: The documentary was tendentious, ignoring every opposing study.

definition: eager to fight; aggressively defiant
example: The truculent customer demanded to see the manager.

definition: superficially plausible but actually wrong
example: His specious argument fell apart under scrutiny.

definition: to impair the quality of; to make ineffective
example: Procedural errors vitiated the entire trial.

definition: stubbornly refusing to change one's mind
example: The obdurate board rejected every proposed amendment.
